body.p: Status of the Application

By this Amendment, Claims 1, 2, 6, and 7 have been amended for clarity, and Claim 5 is canceled without prejudice or disclaimer. No new subject matter has been added. Thus, Claims 1- 4, 6, and 7 are presently pending, with Claims 1, 6, and 7 being independent.
Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the claims in view of the presented amendments and accompanying remarks. Formalities

Applicant thanks the Examiner for confirming consideration of the reference cited in the Information Disclosure Statement filed June 20, 2023. Certification and Request for Consideration under AFCP 2.0

Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner consider the instant Amendment based on the After Final Consideration Pilot (AFCP) 2.0. The AFCP 2.0 authorizes extra time for examiners to consider responses filed after a final rejection under 37 C.F.R. § 1.116 during the duration of the pilot if the Examiner believes that such a response may lead to allowance of the application with only limited further search and/or consideration by the Examiner. Applicant respectfully submits that the instant Amendment overcomes the current cited references and requires only a limited further search and/or consideration by the Examiner. An AFCP 2.0 Request form has been filed herewith.
Claims 1-7 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as purportedly being unpatentable over
Ratnasingam (US 9,672,734), in view of Abe (US 2019/0113914), and in further view of Watanabe
Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections for at least the following reasons and
discusses independent Claim 1 as an example.
Without any admissions, independent Claim 1 has been amended to recite features similar
to those previously recited in now-cancelled dependent Claim 5:
A vehicle control device configured to control a vehicle, comprising:
an information provision device configured to provide information to a
driver of the vehicle;

a processor, during automated driving control of the vehicle, configured to: perform the automated driving control by automatically performing a driving operation of the vehicle relating to a driving plan of the vehicle control device, the automated driving control comprising operations relating to at least one of acceleration, steering, and braking, according to
the driving plan;
provide, through the information provision device to the driver, a driving event that is to occur at a point ahead in a direction of advance from
a current point, based on an automated driving plan;
judge a suitability of a driver driving operation corresponding to the driving event being performed by the driver at a point before the point of
the driving event;

provide the driver with judgment information indicating that the driver not perform the driver driving operation, based on the judging of the suitability determining that performing the driver driving operation is unsuitable according to the driving plan being executed by the vehicle
control device; and

when the driver driving operation corresponding to the driving event is a lane change, provide to the driver, together with lane change inhibiting information, distance information from the current point to a point where a lane to be changed to is to at least one of disappear due
to a lane reduction and be unable to be driven.

At a minimum, the proposed Ratnasingam-Abe-Watanabe combination does not disclose, teach, or suggest "when the driver driving operation corresponding to the driving event is a lane change, provide to the driver, together with lane change inhibiting information, distance information from the current point to a point where a lane to be changed to is to at least one of disappear due to a lane reduction and be unable to be driven," as recited in Claim 1.

The Office Action acknowledges that Ratnasingam and Abe do not teach the cited features of Claim 1. See Office Action, p. 11-12 (citing Claim 5 prior to the present amendments). Instead, the Office Action relies on Watanabe as allegedly disclosing these features. Applicant respectfully submits that Watanabe does not make up for at least the above-discussed deficiencies of Ratnasingam and Abe.

Watanabe discloses, referring to FIG. 71, an image generator that "generates an image in which the inexecutable action ('lane change to right' 1202) is displayed in a display manner, different from the display manner of the other executable actions, where the icon indicating the inexecutable action is grayed out or the luminance of the icon is reduced":
FIG. 71
SVG {EMBED HERE} 2.3333.063 entinformation"
Watanabe, FIG. 71 (annotated) and [0597].

According to Watanabe, the "image illustrated in FIG. 71 indicates that the occupant selects 'lane change to right' 1202 which cannot be executed by the occupant. When the information indicating that 'lane change to right' 1202 is selected by the occupant is input from operation input unit 1050, image generator 1041b updates the frame of the icon for selected 'lane change to right' 1202 in boldface, and adds a negative action basis that 'lane change to right' 1202 cannot be executed in this image. Id. at [0598]. Watanabe further discloses that when "there are start and end points of a lane end section within a predetermined distance, the distances to the start and end points of the lane end section are classified into a plurality of predetermined levels, and the numerical values of the classified levels are stored in the part of the 'distance to start/end point of lane end section'. When there are no start and end points of a lane end section within the predetermined distance, '0' is stored in the part of the 'distance to start/end point of lane end section'." Watanabe, [0392].
That is, at best, Watanabe discloses classifying distances of a lane end section into levels and displaying an icon indicating an inexecutable action.

To the extent the Office is attempting to equate the icon indicating the inexecutable action of Watanabe to the claimed "lane change inhibiting information" and the start and end points of the lane end section of Watanabe to the claimed "distance information", Claim 1 recites "when the driver driving operation corresponding to the driving event is a lane change, provide to the driver, together with lane change inhibiting information, distance information from the current point to a point where a lane to be changed to is to at least one of disappear due to a lane reduction and be unable to be driven." Watanabe does not disclose displaying the start and end points of the lane end section or the classified levels to the user, much less display this information together with the icon indicating the inexecutable action. Therefore, Watanabe's purported disclosure of an icon indicating an inexecutable action does not disclose the claimed "lane change inhibiting information".
Consequently, Watanabe does not disclose, teach, or suggest at least the cited features recited in Claim 1.

Thus, even assuming for the sake of argument only that the proposed Ratnasingam-Abe- Watanabe combination would have been proper, which Applicant does not concede, the proposed combination does not disclose, teach, or suggest all features recited in Claim 1.
In view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that Claim 1 is patentable over the cited references and requests withdrawal of the rejection.

To the extent that independent Claims 6 and 7 recite features similar to the above-noted features of Claim 1, Applicant submits that Claims 6 and 7 are patentable for at least reasons similar to those discussed above with respect to Claim 1.
Applicant respectfully submits that dependent Claims 2-4 are patentable due to their respective dependencies, as well as for their additional features. This should not be construed as

an acquiescence to Examiner's interpretation of the claims, or reading of those claim elements on the prior art, and Applicant expressly reserves the right to establish the patentability of those additional claim limitations, should the need arise.
Dependent Claim 5 is canceled without prejudice or disclaimer by the instant Amendment, thus rendering its rejections moot.

In view of the above, reconsideration and allowance of this application are now believed to be in order, and such actions are hereby solicited.
